title: Cap. III Rej. Rat. 1: sufficient aids fail for pagans/infants — Augustine De nat.
pass_a_gloss: Further, those who attribute to God this will of good pleasure concerning the salvation of all gather it from this, that he gives to all sufficient helps for obtaining salvation: which yet they will never prove either of the Pagans, to whom the name of Christ and the light of the Gospel never became known, or of their infants who die without baptism (to say nothing of others). Augustine expressly teaches that many are damned who could not be justified and saved, On Nature and Grace, chapters 8 and 9.
pass_b_english: Those who put on God a good-pleasure will for everyone's salvation infer it from "sufficient helps for all" — yet they never prove that of pagans who never heard Christ's name or Gospel light, nor of their infants dying unbaptized (never mind the rest). Augustine says plainly many are damned who could not be justified and saved (On Nature and Grace 8–9).
source_text: Porro, qui Deo tribuunt hanc voluntatem beneplaciti circa omnium salutem, id inde colligunt, quod omnibus det sufficientia auxilia ad salutem obtinendam: quod tamen nec de Paganis, quibus Christi nomen & Evangelii lumen nunquam innotuit, nec de infantibus illorum qui absque baptismo moriuntur, (ut de aliis nihil dicam) unquam probabunt. Augustinus diserte docet, damnari multos qui justificari & salvari non potuerint, De Nat. & grat. cap. 8. & 9.
